transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to always make time for things I enjoyed... painting, hiking, singing in my choir, and going to Sunday family gatherings. But lately, even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I can't seem to care about any of it anymore.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest?
I'd say it's been building for about eight months now. It really started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at work.
During these past eight months, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day on most days?

Yes, I have. Most days, actually. It's... well, it just feels like there's this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right in the middle of a classroom full of students, or just at home with my husband, and I still feel completely hollow. Like I'm just... close to tears most of the time.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I've never felt unusually high or energetic like that. I get stressed or a little irritable sometimes, just from normal life stuff, but nothing extreme. It's really just been this constant low.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yes, I have. Sometimes... on late nights in the studio, I catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief if I didn't wake up. I haven't made a plan to hurt myself or do anything like that, but those thoughts really scare me. They scared me enough that I finally told my husband I just couldn't keep handling them alone anymore.
Have you noticed a significant drop in your energy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired, but I wouldn't say it's a huge drop in my energy. It's more just... the feeling of being down all the time is exhausting, you know? But physically, I can still get through my day at work and everything. It's just hard to care about it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions during this period?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I mean, my job at the school keeps me pretty busy, and I'm still able to focus on what I need to do. Making decisions hasn't been any harder than usual. It's really just the mood and the thoughts that are the problem.
How has your sleep been during these eight months?

It's been all over the place for months, honestly. I'll go to bed and just lie awake, replaying grant details in my head. Then I usually end up waking up around three or four in the morning. And even on the nights when I do manage to sleep a bit longer, I get up feeling like I never rested at all.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite during these eight months?

No, my appetite has been pretty normal. I mean, I still eat my regular meals and everything. I haven't really noticed any weight changes or feeling more or less hungry than usual... so, yeah, eating hasn't really been an issue for me.
During this period, have you been feeling unusually worthless or excessively guilty about things?

Yes, I have been feeling like that. It's... it's mostly related to work. When anything goes wrong with the curriculum project I'm helping with, even just a small mistake or delay, I get this overwhelming feeling that I'm letting the students down. And then I start thinking about my parents, and how much they sacrificed for me to get my degree and have this opportunity... and I just feel like I'm completely wasting it all. It's a heavy feeling of guilt that just kind of sits there.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to function at work, at home, and in your relationships?

It's interfered quite a bit, honestly. At work, I've actually missed several teaching sessions lately, and I've been avoiding the student workshops. I just... I can't keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. 

And at home, it's affecting things there, too. My husband has had to step in a lot more to handle things. I tend to withdraw from our family plans, and I just don't feel safe trying to push through everything alone right now.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or feeling so restless that you cannot sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I think I'm moving and speaking at my normal pace. And I don't feel restless or anything... I can sit still without a problem. So, no, no changes there.
